caption: Energy per run of the AI and the human implementation in each task. The bar and its label give the median and each point is one run. Every task has its own y-axis starting at 0, and the panel title says which treatment has the higher median and by what factor. Within a group the runs differ very little (coefficient of variation at most 1.84%), so the points overlap and a box plot would shrink to a line. The shape of each distribution is shown in the density figure.

Deviation of the energy of each run from its group mean against the GPU temperature at the start of the run, with a least-squares line per group and its R² in the panel title. The start temperature ranged from 34 to 44 °C and depends on the run before. It explains up to 85% of the variation within a group (ZAPBench human, +0.40% energy per °C).

Distribution of the energy per run for each task and treatment as a kernel density estimate, each panel on its own scale. The ticks at the bottom are the single runs and the label gives the coefficient of variation (CV), as in the descriptive energy table. Runs that lie very close together share one darker tick. With 10 or 20 runs per group, a small bump or shoulder in a curve rests on only a few runs.

Normal Q-Q plots of the CPU utilization and GPU utilization per run (rows) in each task, with AI and human in the same panel and the values standardized within each task and treatment. The shaded band is the 95% pointwise band of a normal sample of the same size around the identity line. The text gives the Shapiro-Wilk p-value of each treatment, in bold where normality is rejected (p < 0.05). Implementations that do not use the GPU stay at 0% in every run and are not tested.

Normal Q-Q plots of the energy, execution time and memory increase per run (rows) in each task, with AI and human in the same panel and the values standardized within each task and treatment. The shaded band is the 95% pointwise band of a normal sample of the same size around the identity line. The text gives the Shapiro-Wilk p-value of each treatment, in bold where normality is rejected (p < 0.05). Execution time is measured on the 0.2 s sampling grid of EnergiBridge, so runs of equal length form steps.

RQ2 per task, (a) execution time, (b) mean CPU utilization, (c) mean GPU utilization and (d) memory increase per run of the AI and the human implementation. The bar and its label give the median, each point is one run and the panel title says which treatment has the higher median and by what factor. Time and memory have their own y-axis from 0 in every panel, CPU and GPU utilization share one 0 to 100% scale. The dashed line in (b) marks one fully busy hardware thread (6.25% of the 16 threads of the Intel Core i9-11900KF). scRNA-seq and COVID-19 run on the CPU only, so their GPU panels in (c) are empty. Memory is the increase of the used main memory of the whole machine from the start to the peak of a run, without GPU memory.

Energy per run against mean CPU utilization for each task and treatment, each panel on its own scales. The panel title gives Pearson's r or Spearman's rho with its 95% interval, and the line is a least-squares fit with its 95% band where the coefficient is Pearson's r.

Energy per run against mean GPU utilization for each task and treatment, each panel on its own scales. The panel title gives Pearson's r or Spearman's rho with its 95% interval, and the line is a least-squares fit with its 95% band where the coefficient is Pearson's r. scRNA-seq AI, scRNA-seq human, COVID-19 AI, COVID-19 human and GIFT-Eval AI do not use the GPU, stay at 0% in every run and are not shown.

Energy per run against memory increase for each task and treatment, each panel on its own scales. The panel title gives Pearson's r or Spearman's rho with its 95% interval, and the line is a least-squares fit with its 95% band where the coefficient is Pearson's r.

Energy per run against execution time for each task and treatment, each panel on its own scales. The panel title gives Pearson's r or Spearman's rho with its 95% interval, and the line is a least-squares fit with its 95% band where the coefficient is Pearson's r. Execution time is measured on the 0.2 s sampling grid of EnergiBridge. In scRNA-seq AI, scRNA-seq human and COVID-19 AI the run lengths fall on only 2 to 4 steps of this grid, and one sample more also adds one more interval of energy, so part of the correlation in these groups comes from the grid.

Correlation of the energy per run with each performance metric, per task and treatment. The point is the coefficient and the line its 95% interval. Filled points are Pearson's r and open points Spearman's rho, which is used where one of the two variables is not normal. Groups in which a metric is the same in every run have no coefficient. The exact values are in the RQ3 table.

Ratio of the AI value to the human value for every variable and task, on one shared log axis. For energy, time, CPU, GPU, memory and power the ratio is that of the medians per run. EQR is the energy-to-quality ratio built from the means, and a value below 1 means AI needs less energy for the quality it reaches. All 95% bootstrap intervals are narrower than the points and are given in the test tables. Mean power is shown because energy is power times time, but it is not tested.
